#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
# integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they cannot
  # run (no sandbox-exec / already-sandboxed host / HOME outside /Users) —
  # the skip lands in the job log, never silent; this leg is where they
  # actually execute.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cube-kernel-live:
    name: Cube kernel live (macOS)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: dart test cube backends (live kernel legs)
        run: dart test test/cube/backends

  static:
    name: Static gates
    runs-on:…

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate

    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env]
    if: always()

    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure
        run: |
          for r in "${{ needs.static.result }}" "${{ needs.test-core.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}" "${{ needs.guards.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}" "${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.test-faui.result }}" "${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"; do
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              echo "Quality gate FAILED (a leg is $r)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already
  # records started/completed per step — dump it as a summary table plus a
  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

blocks.text:
Confirmed. With mounts `[deny /Users/a/.ssh, rw /Users/a]` (deny child listed before rw parent):
- Guard: `/Users/a/.ssh/[REDACTED:Credential File]` → deny (longest-prefix wins).
- Kernel profile under P1 last-match-wins: last matching file-read rule for `/Users/a/.ssh/[REDACTED:Credential File]` is `(allow file-read* (subpath "/Users/a"))` → READ ALLOWED.

Before this PR, rw emitted no read allow, so the last matching read rule was the deny — parity held for reads. After this PR, a nested deny mount's READ protection is silently voided in the kernel when the rw parent is listed after it. (Writes had this hole already; ro parents had it too.)

This is security-relevant: `deny` mounts are the high-value protection (`~/.ssh` under an rw home). IMPORTANT — arguably BLOCKING. The ticket explicitly scopes: "Make the profile match the policy object" and IT1 claims "guard verdict == profile rule verdict" for every access level. The PR's own parity test claims parity but only tests flat siblings. Given the guard's documented semantics ("longest matching mount wins", order-independent), the kernel emission should sort mounts by ascending path depth (or the parity test should cover nesting). I'd call it IMPORTANT leaning BLOCKING... The severity rubric: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug, security issue... This is a potential security hole but conditional (requires nested deny-under-rw with specific ordering; writes already had it; the ticket didn't cover nesting; the threat model is the agent's own shell inside the sandbox — a deny mount is defense-in-depth). For nested mounts declared child-before-parent, the new `readWrite` read-allow lands *after* the child's deny and voids it **for reads** — a divergence this fix newly introduces (before, `rw` emitted no read rule, so the deny held):

```yaml
mounts:
  - {path: /Users/a/.ssh, access: deny}
  - {path: /Users/a,     access: readWrite}
```

Verified against this branch — the profile ends with:

```
(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users/a/.ssh"))
(allow file-read* (subpath "/Users/a"))      ← later, wins under P1
```

so the kernel **allows** reading `/Users/a/.ssh/id_rsa` while `accessFor` returns `deny`. `rw $HOME` + `deny ~/.ssh` is the canonical cube config shape, and the guard's order-independence gives users no reason to sequence mounts defensively. final ordered = [...mounts]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.path.length.compareTo(b.path.length));
for (final mount in ordered) {

}

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/718
- **Title**: fix(cube): rw mounts emit file-read* allow in SBPL — kernel reads under read-denied prefixes
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/709-cube-rw-reads` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +565
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T23:30:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T09:50:12Z

## PR Description

Fixes #709

## What

An `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix is now both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants. `_mountRules` (`lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart`) emitted only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite`; under the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))` the later blanket deny won, so every rw mount below `/Users` was kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable — file tools passed, wrapped shells got `Operation not permitted` (lanes could not run `dart pub get` / `dart test`).

- **readWrite emission**: emits BOTH `(allow file-read*)` and `(allow file-write*)`, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings (AC1). The `/Users` blanket deny and the Dart fs guard are untouched — the profile now matches the policy object.
- **P1 (ordering)**: the stale "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity" comment is replaced with the observed semantics — the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class, so rule order is load-bearing (mount rules emit after the curated denies; AC5). Apple's shipped docs do not cover conflict resolution (`sandbox(7)` documents the facility only), so the ordering is pinned empirically by the profile tests and the live macOS leg.
- **P2 (literal paths + symlink nodes)**: documented at `_resolvedVariants` — the variants cover firmware-symlink targets but cannot cover the symlink node itself; reads through the `/etc` spelling stay denied, git-over-https keeps needing `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (unchanged by this card, per its non-goals).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` — readWrite read-allow emission + P1/P2 documentation (AC1, AC5).
- `test/cube/backends/backends_test.dart` — UT1 (rw under denied prefix → both allows, both spellings, allow ordered after the deny), UT2 (ro/deny emission frozen byte-identical, AC4), E1 (rw mount on the denied prefix root itself), E2 (ro+rw twin stopgap stays deterministic — last entry wins per class), REG1 (linux unshare / windows job / no-op backends unchanged, AC4).
- `test/cube/backends/sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` (new) — IT1: guard verdict == profile-replay verdict (P1 last-match-wins) across ro/rw/deny/workspace/unmapped probes, plus E3 pins (`/etc/hosts` literal spelling stays denied; `/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_rw_live_test.dart` (new) — E2E1: through a real `sandbox-exec` wrap, a file under an rw-mounted read-denied prefix is READ (AC2) and still WRITABLE (AC3), and the `/Users` deny keeps blocking non-mounted paths. Skips are always NAMED (no sandbox-exec / host itself sandboxed — nested profiles intersect / HOME not under `/Users` / cannot stage).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_live_test.dart` — the pre-existing live suite now also skips with a named reason when the host is itself sandboxed (it used to run and get confounded on such hosts).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `cube-kernel-live` (macos-latest) leg running `dart test test/cube/backends` so the live E2E actually executes somewhere; gated on `core`, 10-min timeout, read-only perms.

Verified locally on the l1-dev lane host: full `test/cube/` tree 292 passed + 7 named skips (the live kernel legs — this host is itself inside a cube, exactly the confound the named skip documents); UT1/parity/E1/E2 confirmed RED against the unfixed emission before the fix. Threshold/ratchet files: not touched (measured CRAP max and coverage floor do not move; changed-line coverage is exercised by the new tests).

## Remaining / not in this card

- Same audit for `linux_unshare.dart` / `windows_job.dart` code paths (REG1 asserts their current behavior unchanged; if a semantics change is ever wanted there it is a follow-up card per the issue's tiering).
- Symlink-node readability for firmware roots (`/etc` itself) — documented-only by design (P2): widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug.
- The ro+rw twin mounts in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` stay as-is: harmless after the fix (E2 proves determinism) and still needed for hosts running the pre-fix backend; retiring them is an owner-side ops change once this ships.
- Ratchet/threshold files: not touched (threshold not moved).

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `rw` read-allow re-opens nested `deny` mounts when the parent is listed after the child — kernel profile diverges from the guard's longest-prefix-wins**

This PR's stated goal is "make the profile match the policy object", but the emission still iterates mounts in **list order** while the kernel applies the **last** matching rule (P1) and the Dart guard resolves by **longest prefix, order-independent** (`CubeFsPolicy.accessFor`, documented in `docs/cubes.md:103`: "The longest matching mount wins"; AGENTS.md promises deny-wins).

For nested mounts declared child-before-parent, the new `readWrite` read-allow lands *after* the child's deny and voids it **for reads** — a divergence this fix newly introduces (before, `rw` emitted no read rule, so the deny held):

```yaml
mounts:
  - {path: /Users/a/.ssh, access: deny}
  - {path: /Users/a,     access: readWrite}
```

Verified against this branch — the profile ends with:

```
(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users/a/.ssh"))
(allow file-read* (subpath "/Users/a"))      ← later, wins under P1
```

so the kernel **allows** reading `/Users/a/.ssh/[REDACTED:Credential File]` while `accessFor` returns `deny`. `rw $HOME` + `deny ~/.ssh` is the canonical cube config shape, and the guard's order-independence gives users no reason to sequence mounts defensively. (The same hole pre-existed for writes and `ro` parents — the read side is what this PR changes.)

Cheap fix that also repairs the pre-existing write/`ro` hole: emit mounts **stable-sorted by ascending path depth** (deepest prefix last), so kernel last-match-wins then approximates the guard's longest-prefix-wins:

```dart
final ordered = [...mounts]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.path.length.compareTo(b.path.length));
for (final mount in ordered) {
  _mountRules(buffer, mount);
}
```

and add a nested-mount probe (deny child + rw/ro parent, declared child-first) to `sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` — IT1 currently covers only flat sibling mounts, which is why this passes green.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-20):

The parity spec mounts only `ro-cache`, `rw-cache` and `vault`; nothing covers `/etc/ssl`. # gh-709: fix(cube): rw mounts lose file-read* under read-denied prefixes — readWrite emits no read allow in SBPL

## Description

## Goal — cube rw mounts are kernel-readable (v1)
One sentence: **an `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix becomes both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox**, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants.
Today `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules` emits only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite` — no `file-read*` allow. Under the curated read confinement (blanket `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))`) the later blanket deny wins, so every rw mount below `/Users` is **kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable**: file tools work, wrapped shells get `Operation not permitted`. Live evidence on l1-dev: `ls /Users/agents/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev` → EPERM with the rw mount present; lanes cannot run `dart pub get` / `dart test`.

## Why this framing
- The shipped stopgap — ro+rw **twin mounts** in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` (ro twin emits the read allow, the rw twin re-allows writes over the twin's deny-write) — is retracted as the long-term answer: it double-lists every mount and relies on rule ORDER rather than semantics.
- "Make the profile match the policy object" — not "loosen the read confinement". The blanket `/Users` deny stays.

## Architecture
Subject separation (each capability names its subject):
- **Dart fs guard** (`lib/src/cube/runtime/cube_fs_guard.dart`, `CubeFsPolicy.accessFor`) — already correct for rw (read+write). Untouched.
- **Kernel SBPL profile** (`macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules`) — the fix target.
- **Other backends**: `linux_unshare.dart` and `windows_job.dart`/`no_op_backend.dart` must be audited for the same asymmetry (bind-mount ro vs rw for unshare; no-op degrades to policy mode by design).

Pinned platform facts (load-bearing, each with a positive AND negative test):
- **P1 — SBPL ordering**: the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class (`file-read*` / `file-write*`). The existing code comment claims "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity: the subpath allow wins" — **observed false** in practice (deny `/Users` beats nothing-later; a later allow wins). Fix the comment while fixing the emission.
- **P2 — literal-path matching + symlink traversal**: opening `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` requires reading the `/etc` symlink node, which `(deny file-read* (subpath "/etc"))` blocks — an `(allow file-read* (subpath "/etc/ssl"))` does NOT help; only the `/private/etc/ssl` spelling works. `_resolvedVariants` already emits both spellings; document that it does not (and cannot) cover the symlink node itself. Git over https therefore still needs `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` — unchanged by this card.

## Capability surface (mount access ⇄ emitted kernel rules)
| `spec.filesystem.mounts` access | Dart guard | macOS SBPL today | macOS SBPL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ro` | read | allow read + deny write | unchanged |
| `deny` | none | deny read + deny write | unchanged |
| `rw` | read+write | **allow write only** | **allow read + allow write** |

Tiering: **core** — the `readWrite` emission fix on macOS + the P1 comment correction; **second tier** — same audit for the linux/windows backends (follow-up card if they need code); **excluded** — any change to the `/Users` blanket deny, any symlink-node auto-allow for firmware roots (P2 documented, not solved here; rationale: widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — For a spec with an `rw` mount under a denied read prefix, the staged profile contains `(allow file-read*)` AND `(allow file-write*)` for that mount, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings. (UT hook: profile string assert.)

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING (still open from the previous review — branch unchanged): `rw` read-allow re-opens nested `deny` mounts when the parent is listed after the child — kernel profile diverges from the guard's longest-prefix-wins**

This PR's stated goal is "make the profile match the policy object", but the emission still iterates mounts in **list order** while the kernel applies the **last** matching rule (P1) and the Dart guard resolves by **longest prefix, order-independent** (`CubeFsPolicy.accessFor`, documented in `docs/cubes.md:103`: "The longest matching mount wins"; AGENTS.md promises deny-wins).

For nested mounts declared child-before-parent, the new `readWrite` read-allow lands *after* the child's deny and voids it **for reads** — a divergence this fix newly introduces (before, `rw` emitted no read rule, so the deny held):

```yaml
mounts:
  - {path: /Users/a/.ssh, access: deny}
  - {path: /Users/a,     access: readWrite}
```

Re-verified against the current head of this branch — the profile's read rules for that tree are:

```
(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users/a/.ssh"))
(allow file-read* (subpath "/Users/a"))      ← later, wins under P1
```

so the kernel **allows** reading `/Users/a/.ssh/id_rsa` while `accessFor` returns `deny`. `rw $HOME` + `deny ~/.ssh` is the canonical cube config shape, and the guard's order-independence gives users no reason to sequence mounts defensively. (The same hole pre-existed for writes and `ro` parents — the read side is what this PR changes.)

Cheap fix that also repairs the pre-existing write/`ro` hole: emit mounts **stable-sorted by ascending path depth** (deepest prefix last), so kernel last-match-wins then approximates the guard's longest-prefix-wins:

```dart
final ordered = [...mounts]
  ..sort((a, b) => a.path.length.compareTo(b.path.length));
for (final mount in ordered) {
  _mountRules(buffer, mount);
}
```

and add a nested-mount probe (deny child + rw/ro parent, declared child-first) to `sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` — IT1 currently covers only flat sibling mounts, which is why this passes green.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1_nested_mount_ordering.md"}

That may be a deliberate trade-off (macOS-minute cost / flake exposure), but the ticket's test plan says "a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green" and the PR description frames this leg as where the live guarantee is enforced — silent non-gating should at least be an explicit decision.

So at `/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` **both** sides deny (guard: no mount matches → deny; profile: the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/private/etc"))` matches), and the case only re-proves "unmapped path under a curated deny". The PR description's "E3 pins (`/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable)" is not what this test shows.

2. A *real* `/private`-spelling readability pin can't live in this parity harness at all: add a mount `{path: /etc/ssl, access: rw}` and the kernel allows `/private/etc/ssl/...` (the emitted `/private` variant) while the lexical guard still denies it — an intentional guard↔profile divergence (kernel resolves firmware symlinks, the guard judges the written form). Worth one sentence in `_resolvedVariants`' P2 doc so the next parity audit doesn't rediscover it as a bug.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: scope gate skips the live leg on `shared`-only changes, unlike the sibling core legs**

```yaml
if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'
```

Every other core-scoped leg (`test-core`, `coverage-gate`, `guards`, `hostile-env`, `cli-visual-settings`) triggers on `core == 'true' || shared == 'true'`. A PR touching only root/shared files — e.g. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` itself, `pubspec.yaml`, the cube schema — classifies as `shared`, and this leg silently skips, so e.g. a future workflow edit to *this very job* never gets exercised by it. Consider:

```yaml
if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
```

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/709-cube-rw-reads` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T23:30:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T10:49:56Z

## PR Description

Fixes #709

## What

An `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix is now both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants. `_mountRules` (`lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart`) emitted only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite`; under the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))` the later blanket deny won, so every rw mount below `/Users` was kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable — file tools passed, wrapped shells got `Operation not permitted` (lanes could not run `dart pub get` / `dart test`).

- **readWrite emission**: emits BOTH `(allow file-read*)` and `(allow file-write*)`, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings (AC1). The `/Users` blanket deny and the Dart fs guard are untouched — the profile now matches the policy object.
- **P1 (ordering)**: the stale "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity" comment is replaced with the observed semantics — the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class, so rule order is load-bearing (mount rules emit after the curated denies; AC5). Apple's shipped docs do not cover conflict resolution (`sandbox(7)` documents the facility only), so the ordering is pinned empirically by the profile tests and the live macOS leg.
- **P2 (literal paths + symlink nodes)**: documented at `_resolvedVariants` — the variants cover firmware-symlink targets but cannot cover the symlink node itself; reads through the `/etc` spelling stay denied, git-over-https keeps needing `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (unchanged by this card, per its non-goals).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` — readWrite read-allow emission + P1/P2 documentation (AC1, AC5).
- `test/cube/backends/backends_test.dart` — UT1 (rw under denied prefix → both allows, both spellings, allow ordered after the deny), UT2 (ro/deny emission frozen byte-identical, AC4), E1 (rw mount on the denied prefix root itself), E2 (ro+rw twin stopgap stays deterministic — last entry wins per class), REG1 (linux unshare / windows job / no-op backends unchanged, AC4).
- `test/cube/backends/sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` (new) — IT1: guard verdict == profile-replay verdict (P1 last-match-wins) across ro/rw/deny/workspace/unmapped probes, plus E3 pins (`/etc/hosts` literal spelling stays denied; `/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_rw_live_test.dart` (new) — E2E1: through a real `sandbox-exec` wrap, a file under an rw-mounted read-denied prefix is READ (AC2) and still WRITABLE (AC3), and the `/Users` deny keeps blocking non-mounted paths. Skips are always NAMED (no sandbox-exec / host itself sandboxed — nested profiles intersect / HOME not under `/Users` / cannot stage).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_live_test.dart` — the pre-existing live suite now also skips with a named reason when the host is itself sandboxed (it used to run and get confounded on such hosts).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `cube-kernel-live` (macos-latest) leg running `dart test test/cube/backends` so the live E2E actually executes somewhere; gated on `core`, 10-min timeout, read-only perms.

Verified locally on the l1-dev lane host: full `test/cube/` tree 292 passed + 7 named skips (the live kernel legs — this host is itself inside a cube, exactly the confound the named skip documents); UT1/parity/E1/E2 confirmed RED against the unfixed emission before the fix. Threshold/ratchet files: not touched (measured CRAP max and coverage floor do not move; changed-line coverage is exercised by the new tests).

## Remaining / not in this card

- Same audit for `linux_unshare.dart` / `windows_job.dart` code paths (REG1 asserts their current behavior unchanged; if a semantics change is ever wanted there it is a follow-up card per the issue's tiering).
- Symlink-node readability for firmware roots (`/etc` itself) — documented-only by design (P2): widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug.
- The ro+rw twin mounts in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` stay as-is: harmless after the fix (E2 proves determinism) and still needed for hosts running the pre-fix backend; retiring them is an owner-side ops change once this ships.
- Ratchet/threshold files: not touched (threshold not moved).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/718
- **Title**: fix(cube): rw mounts emit file-read* allow in SBPL — kernel reads under read-denied prefixes
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/709-cube-rw-reads` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +565
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T23:30:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T08:43:19Z

## PR Description

Fixes #709

## What

An `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix is now both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants. `_mountRules` (`lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart`) emitted only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite`; under the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))` the later blanket deny won, so every rw mount below `/Users` was kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable — file tools passed, wrapped shells got `Operation not permitted` (lanes could not run `dart pub get` / `dart test`).

- **readWrite emission**: emits BOTH `(allow file-read*)` and `(allow file-write*)`, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings (AC1). The `/Users` blanket deny and the Dart fs guard are untouched — the profile now matches the policy object.
- **P1 (ordering)**: the stale "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity" comment is replaced with the observed semantics — the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class, so rule order is load-bearing (mount rules emit after the curated denies; AC5). Apple's shipped docs do not cover conflict resolution (`sandbox(7)` documents the facility only), so the ordering is pinned empirically by the profile tests and the live macOS leg.
- **P2 (literal paths + symlink nodes)**: documented at `_resolvedVariants` — the variants cover firmware-symlink targets but cannot cover the symlink node itself; reads through the `/etc` spelling stay denied, git-over-https keeps needing `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (unchanged by this card, per its non-goals).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` — readWrite read-allow emission + P1/P2 documentation (AC1, AC5).
- `test/cube/backends/backends_test.dart` — UT1 (rw under denied prefix → both allows, both spellings, allow ordered after the deny), UT2 (ro/deny emission frozen byte-identical, AC4), E1 (rw mount on the denied prefix root itself), E2 (ro+rw twin stopgap stays deterministic — last entry wins per class), REG1 (linux unshare / windows job / no-op backends unchanged, AC4).
- `test/cube/backends/sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` (new) — IT1: guard verdict == profile-replay verdict (P1 last-match-wins) across ro/rw/deny/workspace/unmapped probes, plus E3 pins (`/etc/hosts` literal spelling stays denied; `/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_rw_live_test.dart` (new) — E2E1: through a real `sandbox-exec` wrap, a file under an rw-mounted read-denied prefix is READ (AC2) and still WRITABLE (AC3), and the `/Users` deny keeps blocking non-mounted paths. Skips are always NAMED (no sandbox-exec / host itself sandboxed — nested profiles intersect / HOME not under `/Users` / cannot stage).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_live_test.dart` — the pre-existing live suite now also skips with a named reason when the host is itself sandboxed (it used to run and get confounded on such hosts).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `cube-kernel-live` (macos-latest) leg running `dart test test/cube/backends` so the live E2E actually executes somewhere; gated on `core`, 10-min timeout, read-only perms.

Verified locally on the l1-dev lane host: full `test/cube/` tree 292 passed + 7 named skips (the live kernel legs — this host is itself inside a cube, exactly the confound the named skip documents); UT1/parity/E1/E2 confirmed RED against the unfixed emission before the fix. Threshold/ratchet files: not touched (measured CRAP max and coverage floor do not move; changed-line coverage is exercised by the new tests).

## Remaining / not in this card

- Same audit for `linux_unshare.dart` / `windows_job.dart` code paths (REG1 asserts their current behavior unchanged; if a semantics change is ever wanted there it is a follow-up card per the issue's tiering).
- Symlink-node readability for firmware roots (`/etc` itself) — documented-only by design (P2): widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug.
- The ro+rw twin mounts in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` stay as-is: harmless after the fix (E2 proves determinism) and still needed for hosts running the pre-fix backend; retiring them is an owner-side ops change once this ships.

# gh-709: fix(cube): rw mounts lose file-read* under read-denied prefixes — readWrite emits no read allow in SBPL

## Description

## Goal — cube rw mounts are kernel-readable (v1)
One sentence: **an `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix becomes both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox**, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants.
Today `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules` emits only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite` — no `file-read*` allow. Under the curated read confinement (blanket `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))`) the later blanket deny wins, so every rw mount below `/Users` is **kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable**: file tools work, wrapped shells get `Operation not permitted`. Live evidence on l1-dev: `ls /Users/agents/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev` → EPERM with the rw mount present; lanes cannot run `dart pub get` / `dart test`.

## Why this framing
- The shipped stopgap — ro+rw **twin mounts** in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` (ro twin emits the read allow, the rw twin re-allows writes over the twin's deny-write) — is retracted as the long-term answer: it double-lists every mount and relies on rule ORDER rather than semantics.
- "Make the profile match the policy object" — not "loosen the read confinement". The blanket `/Users` deny stays.

## Architecture
Subject separation (each capability names its subject):
- **Dart fs guard** (`lib/src/cube/runtime/cube_fs_guard.dart`, `CubeFsPolicy.accessFor`) — already correct for rw (read+write). Untouched.
- **Kernel SBPL profile** (`macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules`) — the fix target.
- **Other backends**: `linux_unshare.dart` and `windows_job.dart`/`no_op_backend.dart` must be audited for the same asymmetry (bind-mount ro vs rw for unshare; no-op degrades to policy mode by design).

Pinned platform facts (load-bearing, each with a positive AND negative test):
- **P1 — SBPL ordering**: the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class (`file-read*` / `file-write*`). The existing code comment claims "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity: the subpath allow wins" — **observed false** in practice (deny `/Users` beats nothing-later; a later allow wins). Fix the comment while fixing the emission.
- **P2 — literal-path matching + symlink traversal**: opening `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` requires reading the `/etc` symlink node, which `(deny file-read* (subpath "/etc"))` blocks — an `(allow file-read* (subpath "/etc/ssl"))` does NOT help; only the `/private/etc/ssl` spelling works. `_resolvedVariants` already emits both spellings; document that it does not (and cannot) cover the symlink node itself. Git over https therefore still needs `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` — unchanged by this card.

## Capability surface (mount access ⇄ emitted kernel rules)
| `spec.filesystem.mounts` access | Dart guard | macOS SBPL today | macOS SBPL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ro` | read | allow read + deny write | unchanged |
| `deny` | none | deny read + deny write | unchanged |
| `rw` | read+write | **allow write only** | **allow read + allow write** |

Tiering: **core** — the `readWrite` emission fix on macOS + the P1 comment correction; **second tier** — same audit for the linux/windows backends (follow-up card if they need code); **excluded** — any change to the `/Users` blanket deny, any symlink-node auto-allow for firmware roots (P2 documented, not solved here; rationale: widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — For a spec with an `rw` mount under a denied read prefix, the staged profile contains `(allow file-read*)` AND `(allow file-write*)` for that mount, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings. (UT hook: profile string assert.)
- **AC2** — A kernel-backend wrapped shell can READ a file under an rw mount that sits under a read-denied prefix (E2E, macOS CI leg; today EPERM).
- **AC3** — The same wrapped shell can still WRITE there (AC2's twin — the fix must not cost writes).
- **AC4** — `ro` and `deny` mounts emit byte-identical rule sets before/after (REG guard against emission drift).
- **AC5** — The stale "specificity" comment is gone; the ordering semantics (P1) are documented at `_mountRules`.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT1` profile text: rw mount → both allow lines, both spellings (AC1). `UT2` ro/deny emission frozen (AC4).
- `IT1` `CubePolicyEngine`/fs-guard parity: for every access level, guard verdict == profile rule verdict (subject pair).
- `E2E1` macOS kernel backend: wrapped `head` under an rw-mounted denied-prefix path succeeds (AC2), wrapped append/write succeeds (AC3). Runs only on the macOS CI leg; skipped-leg must be named in the job log, not silent.
- `REG1` non-macOS backends: profile/rule generation for linux/windows/no-op unchanged (AC4) — a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — rw mount whose path equals the denied prefix root itself.
- **E2** — mount list containing BOTH ro and rw entries for the same path (the l1-dev twin stopgap): after the fix the profile must stay deterministic (last-entry-wins per access class) — the stopgap keeps working.
- **E3** — symlinked mount path under `/etc` (P2): read stays denied via the literal spelling — pinned, with the documented `/private` workaround.

## Non-goals
- No change to the Dart fs guard, the `/Users` read confinement, or the tool allowlist.
- No symlink-node readability for firmware roots (P2 stays documented-only).
- Not re-litigating cube preset defaults.

## Open questions
- Confirm P1 (last-match-wins) against Apple's current SBPL docs and pin the doc link in the comment — I verified behavior empirically only.

## References
- Workaround in place: `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` (ro+rw twin blocks, with rationale comments).
- Session evidence: EPERM on `/Users/agents/.pub-cache` reads with rw mount; `/etc/ssl` literal-spelling denial with both-variant allows present.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

Key finding confirmed: the Dart guard (`accessFor`) uses **longest matching mount wins**, while the SBPL profile uses **last matching rule in emission order**. For nested mounts these disagree depending on mount list order:

- Guard: longest prefix wins regardless of order.
- Kernel: last emitted matching rule wins; emission follows mount list order.

Example: mounts = [{path: /a/b, access: deny}, {path: /a, access: rw}]. Guard for /a/b/x: deny (longest match /a/b). Kernel profile: deny-read /a/b then allow-read /a → last match wins → allow read. Divergence — kernel grants read where guard denies. This is a **security-relevant** divergence: a `deny` mount nested under an `rw` (or `ro`) mount, declared before the parent, is silently overridden in the kernel.

Was it pre-existing? For writes: rw emitted allow-write; deny mount emitted deny-write. Order [deny /a/b, rw /a]: deny-write /a/b, allow-write /a → last match allow → write allowed at kernel, guard denies. Yes, pre-existing for writes. For reads: before the fix, rw emitted no read allow, so read of /a/b: deny-read /a/b only → denied → parity. After fix: allow-read /a comes later → allowed → new read divergence. So the PR **introduces** a new guard↔kernel read divergence for nested deny-under-rw/ro declared before the parent. For ro: pre-existing (ro already emitted allow-read). So the divergence class existed for ro; the PR extends it to rw.

Hmm, wait — for ro: [deny /a/b, ro /a] → deny-read /a/b, allow-read /a → kernel allows read, guard denies. Yes pre-existing for ro. So the parity gap predates the PR but the PR widens it and claims IT1 parity "for every access level". The parity test only probes flat sibling mounts, so it doesn't catch this. I'd flag as IMPORTANT: either emit mounts sorted by path depth (deepest last) so last-match-wins approximates longest-prefix-wins, or document/test the limitation. Emission order = list order currently; sorting mounts by prefix length ascending before emission would align semantics. name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # Manual escape hatch: GitHub never runs pull_request workflows on a
  # CONFLICTING PR (no merge commit to run against) — dispatch gates on the
  # PR branch directly: gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure
        run: |
          for r in "${{ needs.static.result }}" "${{ needs.test-core.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}" "${{ needs.guards.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}" "${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.test-faui.result }}" "${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}" \
                   "${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"; do
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              echo "Quality gate FAILED (a leg is $r)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # Issue #194 (point 4): per-step duration telemetry. The jobs API already

  # raw artifact instead of instrumenting every step by hand.
  step-timings:
    name: Per-step timing telemetry
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

But the new `cube-kernel-live` leg itself is not aggregated → its red status doesn't block merge. Whether that's intentional (macOS legs are expensive; skipped outside core PRs anyway) — but the PR's whole point is that this leg "is where they actually execute" as evidence. If it can go red without blocking merge, the E2E1 guarantee is advisory only. Severity: IMPORTANT (workflow gap). Note the precedent: quality-gate includes cli-visual-settings (macos-latest) — so macOS legs ARE aggregated elsewhere. So omitting cube-kernel-live from quality-gate's needs is inconsistent with the repo pattern. IMPORTANT.

Also note: quality-gate's "Fail on any real failure" loop doesn't include cli-visual-settings/build-* either (they're in `needs` so `always()` gate waits for them... wait, actually the loop only checks a subset: static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, integration-mock, hostile-env. It does NOT check cli-visual-settings, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos results in the loop! But they're in `needs:` — with `if: always()`, a failed needed job doesn't auto-fail the gate; the loop decides. Hmm, so build legs failing wouldn't fail the gate either? That seems like an existing oddity — but wait, maybe intentional? Actually if a needs job fails, `needs.X.result` is 'failure' but the loop doesn't check those. So quality-gate would pass even if build-macos fails? That seems like an existing bug in the workflow, not this PR's concern. Not our scope — but the pattern shows adding cube-kernel-live to `needs` alone wouldn't even be checked by the loop; both are needed. Write: blanket deny write, then allow-write workspace (via _allowWorkspaceWrites, emitted after curated denies) → allow. Parity holds.

'ro mount' probe: guard ro → read true, write false. Profile: read: deny /Users then allow-read ro-cache (mount rules emitted after) → true. Write: blanket deny, deny-write ro-cache → false. Parity.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/718
- **Title**: fix(cube): rw mounts emit file-read* allow in SBPL — kernel reads under read-denied prefixes
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/709-cube-rw-reads` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +565
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T23:30:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T09:50:12Z

## PR Description

Fixes #709

## What

An `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix is now both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants. `_mountRules` (`lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart`) emitted only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite`; under the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))` the later blanket deny won, so every rw mount below `/Users` was kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable — file tools passed, wrapped shells got `Operation not permitted` (lanes could not run `dart pub get` / `dart test`).

- **readWrite emission**: emits BOTH `(allow file-read*)` and `(allow file-write*)`, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings (AC1). The `/Users` blanket deny and the Dart fs guard are untouched — the profile now matches the policy object.
- **P1 (ordering)**: the stale "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity" comment is replaced with the observed semantics — the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class, so rule order is load-bearing (mount rules emit after the curated denies; AC5). Apple's shipped docs do not cover conflict resolution (`sandbox(7)` documents the facility only), so the ordering is pinned empirically by the profile tests and the live macOS leg.
- **P2 (literal paths + symlink nodes)**: documented at `_resolvedVariants` — the variants cover firmware-symlink targets but cannot cover the symlink node itself; reads through the `/etc` spelling stay denied, git-over-https keeps needing `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (unchanged by this card, per its non-goals).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` — readWrite read-allow emission + P1/P2 documentation (AC1, AC5).
- `test/cube/backends/backends_test.dart` — UT1 (rw under denied prefix → both allows, both spellings, allow ordered after the deny), UT2 (ro/deny emission frozen byte-identical, AC4), E1 (rw mount on the denied prefix root itself), E2 (ro+rw twin stopgap stays deterministic — last entry wins per class), REG1 (linux unshare / windows job / no-op backends unchanged, AC4).
- `test/cube/backends/sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` (new) — IT1: guard verdict == profile-replay verdict (P1 last-match-wins) across ro/rw/deny/workspace/unmapped probes, plus E3 pins (`/etc/hosts` literal spelling stays denied; `/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_rw_live_test.dart` (new) — E2E1: through a real `sandbox-exec` wrap, a file under an rw-mounted read-denied prefix is READ (AC2) and still WRITABLE (AC3), and the `/Users` deny keeps blocking non-mounted paths. Skips are always NAMED (no sandbox-exec / host itself sandboxed — nested profiles intersect / HOME not under `/Users` / cannot stage).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_live_test.dart` — the pre-existing live suite now also skips with a named reason when the host is itself sandboxed (it used to run and get confounded on such hosts).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `cube-kernel-live` (macos-latest) leg running `dart test test/cube/backends` so the live E2E actually executes somewhere; gated on `core`, 10-min timeout, read-only perms.

Verified locally on the l1-dev lane host: full `test/cube/` tree 292 passed + 7 named skips (the live kernel legs — this host is itself inside a cube, exactly the confound the named skip documents); UT1/parity/E1/E2 confirmed RED against the unfixed emission before the fix. Threshold/ratchet files: not touched (measured CRAP max and coverage floor do not move; changed-line coverage is exercised by the new tests).

## Remaining / not in this card

- Same audit for `linux_unshare.dart` / `windows_job.dart` code paths (REG1 asserts their current behavior unchanged; if a semantics change is ever wanted there it is a follow-up card per the issue's tiering).
- Symlink-node readability for firmware roots (`/etc` itself) — documented-only by design (P2): widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug.
- The ro+rw twin mounts in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` stay as-is: harmless after the fix (E2 proves determinism) and still needed for hosts running the pre-fix backend; retiring them is an owner-side ops change once this ships.
- Ratchet/threshold files: not touched (threshold not moved).

# gh-709: fix(cube): rw mounts lose file-read* under read-denied prefixes — readWrite emits no read allow in SBPL

## Description

## Goal — cube rw mounts are kernel-readable (v1)
One sentence: **an `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix becomes both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox**, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants.
Today `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules` emits only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite` — no `file-read*` allow. Under the curated read confinement (blanket `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))`) the later blanket deny wins, so every rw mount below `/Users` is **kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable**: file tools work, wrapped shells get `Operation not permitted`. Live evidence on l1-dev: `ls /Users/agents/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev` → EPERM with the rw mount present; lanes cannot run `dart pub get` / `dart test`.

## Why this framing
- The shipped stopgap — ro+rw **twin mounts** in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` (ro twin emits the read allow, the rw twin re-allows writes over the twin's deny-write) — is retracted as the long-term answer: it double-lists every mount and relies on rule ORDER rather than semantics.
- "Make the profile match the policy object" — not "loosen the read confinement". The blanket `/Users` deny stays.

## Architecture
Subject separation (each capability names its subject):
- **Dart fs guard** (`lib/src/cube/runtime/cube_fs_guard.dart`, `CubeFsPolicy.accessFor`) — already correct for rw (read+write). Untouched.
- **Kernel SBPL profile** (`macos_sandbox.dart` `_mountRules`) — the fix target.
- **Other backends**: `linux_unshare.dart` and `windows_job.dart`/`no_op_backend.dart` must be audited for the same asymmetry (bind-mount ro vs rw for unshare; no-op degrades to policy mode by design).

Pinned platform facts (load-bearing, each with a positive AND negative test):
- **P1 — SBPL ordering**: the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class (`file-read*` / `file-write*`). The existing code comment claims "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity: the subpath allow wins" — **observed false** in practice (deny `/Users` beats nothing-later; a later allow wins). Fix the comment while fixing the emission.
- **P2 — literal-path matching + symlink traversal**: opening `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` requires reading the `/etc` symlink node, which `(deny file-read* (subpath "/etc"))` blocks — an `(allow file-read* (subpath "/etc/ssl"))` does NOT help; only the `/private/etc/ssl` spelling works. `_resolvedVariants` already emits both spellings; document that it does not (and cannot) cover the symlink node itself. Git over https therefore still needs `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` — unchanged by this card.

## Capability surface (mount access ⇄ emitted kernel rules)
| `spec.filesystem.mounts` access | Dart guard | macOS SBPL today | macOS SBPL after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ro` | read | allow read + deny write | unchanged |
| `deny` | none | deny read + deny write | unchanged |
| `rw` | read+write | **allow write only** | **allow read + allow write** |

Tiering: **core** — the `readWrite` emission fix on macOS + the P1 comment correction; **second tier** — same audit for the linux/windows backends (follow-up card if they need code); **excluded** — any change to the `/Users` blanket deny, any symlink-node auto-allow for firmware roots (P2 documented, not solved here; rationale: widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1** — For a spec with an `rw` mount under a denied read prefix, the staged profile contains `(allow file-read*)` AND `(allow file-write*)` for that mount, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings. (UT hook: profile string assert.)
- **AC2** — A kernel-backend wrapped shell can READ a file under an rw mount that sits under a read-denied prefix (E2E, macOS CI leg; today EPERM).
- **AC3** — The same wrapped shell can still WRITE there (AC2's twin — the fix must not cost writes).
- **AC4** — `ro` and `deny` mounts emit byte-identical rule sets before/after (REG guard against emission drift).
- **AC5** — The stale "specificity" comment is gone; the ordering semantics (P1) are documented at `_mountRules`.

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT1` profile text: rw mount → both allow lines, both spellings (AC1). `UT2` ro/deny emission frozen (AC4).
- `IT1` `CubePolicyEngine`/fs-guard parity: for every access level, guard verdict == profile rule verdict (subject pair).
- `E2E1` macOS kernel backend: wrapped `head` under an rw-mounted denied-prefix path succeeds (AC2), wrapped append/write succeeds (AC3). Runs only on the macOS CI leg; skipped-leg must be named in the job log, not silent.
- `REG1` non-macOS backends: profile/rule generation for linux/windows/no-op unchanged (AC4) — a red REG job blocks merge even when IT/E2E are green.

### Edge / border cases
- **E1** — rw mount whose path equals the denied prefix root itself.
- **E2** — mount list containing BOTH ro and rw entries for the same path (the l1-dev twin stopgap): after the fix the profile must stay deterministic (last-entry-wins per access class) — the stopgap keeps working.
- **E3** — symlinked mount path under `/etc` (P2): read stays denied via the literal spelling — pinned, with the documented `/private` workaround.

## Non-goals
- No change to the Dart fs guard, the `/Users` read confinement, or the tool allowlist.
- No symlink-node readability for firmware roots (P2 stays documented-only).
- Not re-litigating cube preset defaults.

## Open questions
- Confirm P1 (last-match-wins) against Apple's current SBPL docs and pin the doc link in the comment — I verified behavior empirically only.

## References
- Workaround in place: `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` (ro+rw twin blocks, with rationale comments).
- Session evidence: EPERM on `/Users/agents/.pub-cache` reads with rw mount; `/etc/ssl` literal-spelling denial with both-variant allows present.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 718
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/718
- **Title**: fix(cube): rw mounts emit file-read* allow in SBPL — kernel reads under read-denied prefixes
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/709-cube-rw-reads` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 6
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -9
- **Created**: 2026-09-19T23:30:51Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-20T10:49:56Z

## PR Description

Fixes #709

## What

An `rw` mount under a read-denied prefix is now both writable AND readable through the kernel sandbox, matching what the Dart fs-policy layer already grants. `_mountRules` (`lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart`) emitted only `(allow file-write*)` for `CubePathAccess.readWrite`; under the curated `(deny file-read* (subpath "/Users"))` the later blanket deny won, so every rw mount below `/Users` was kernel-unreadable while Dart-guard-readable — file tools passed, wrapped shells got `Operation not permitted` (lanes could not run `dart pub get` / `dart test`).

- **readWrite emission**: emits BOTH `(allow file-read*)` and `(allow file-write*)`, in both `_resolvedVariants` spellings (AC1). The `/Users` blanket deny and the Dart fs guard are untouched — the profile now matches the policy object.
- **P1 (ordering)**: the stale "SBPL resolves conflicts by specificity" comment is replaced with the observed semantics — the kernel applies the LAST matching rule per operation class, so rule order is load-bearing (mount rules emit after the curated denies; AC5). Apple's shipped docs do not cover conflict resolution (`sandbox(7)` documents the facility only), so the ordering is pinned empirically by the profile tests and the live macOS leg.
- **P2 (literal paths + symlink nodes)**: documented at `_resolvedVariants` — the variants cover firmware-symlink targets but cannot cover the symlink node itself; reads through the `/etc` spelling stay denied, git-over-https keeps needing `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/private/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (unchanged by this card, per its non-goals).

## Delivered

- `lib/src/cube/backends/macos_sandbox.dart` — readWrite read-allow emission + P1/P2 documentation (AC1, AC5).
- `test/cube/backends/backends_test.dart` — UT1 (rw under denied prefix → both allows, both spellings, allow ordered after the deny), UT2 (ro/deny emission frozen byte-identical, AC4), E1 (rw mount on the denied prefix root itself), E2 (ro+rw twin stopgap stays deterministic — last entry wins per class), REG1 (linux unshare / windows job / no-op backends unchanged, AC4).
- `test/cube/backends/sbpl_guard_parity_test.dart` (new) — IT1: guard verdict == profile-replay verdict (P1 last-match-wins) across ro/rw/deny/workspace/unmapped probes, plus E3 pins (`/etc/hosts` literal spelling stays denied; `/private/etc/ssl/...` mount spelling readable).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_rw_live_test.dart` (new) — E2E1: through a real `sandbox-exec` wrap, a file under an rw-mounted read-denied prefix is READ (AC2) and still WRITABLE (AC3), and the `/Users` deny keeps blocking non-mounted paths. Skips are always NAMED (no sandbox-exec / host itself sandboxed — nested profiles intersect / HOME not under `/Users` / cannot stage).
- `test/cube/backends/macos_sandbox_live_test.dart` — the pre-existing live suite now also skips with a named reason when the host is itself sandboxed (it used to run and get confounded on such hosts).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new `cube-kernel-live` (macos-latest) leg running `dart test test/cube/backends` so the live E2E actually executes somewhere; gated on `core`, 10-min timeout, read-only perms.

Verified locally on the l1-dev lane host: full `test/cube/` tree 292 passed + 7 named skips (the live kernel legs — this host is itself inside a cube, exactly the confound the named skip documents); UT1/parity/E1/E2 confirmed RED against the unfixed emission before the fix. Threshold/ratchet files: not touched (measured CRAP max and coverage floor do not move; changed-line coverage is exercised by the new tests).

## Remaining / not in this card

- Same audit for `linux_unshare.dart` / `windows_job.dart` code paths (REG1 asserts their current behavior unchanged; if a semantics change is ever wanted there it is a follow-up card per the issue's tiering).
- Symlink-node readability for firmware roots (`/etc` itself) — documented-only by design (P2): widening `/etc` readability is a security decision, not an emission bug.
- The ro+rw twin mounts in `.fah/cubes/l1-dev.yaml` stay as-is: harmless after the fix (E2 proves determinism) and still needed for hosts running the pre-fix backend; retiring them is an owner-side ops change once this ships.
- Ratchet/threshold files: not touched (threshold not moved).
